pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why do we read books?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to direct and inferential questions from a text correctly

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. respond to direct and inferential questions from a text correctly
   In simple words: practise until you can respond to direct and inferential questions from a text correctly. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading.
4. Show that you can: respond to direct and inferential questions from a text correctly

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss and relate ideas to their experiences collaboratively with peers,
2. Read a text independently and retell it in own words,
3. Learning to Learn is enhanced as the learner uses skimming and scanning skills to obtain information from a text.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we read books?
2. Why should we make notes when reading?
3. What makes you a good reader?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. respond to direct and inferential questions from a text correctly

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
